stem: Who holds power to appoint the nominees from Anglo-Indian Community in the lok Sabha?
expl: At the time of this question, under Article 331, the President had the power to nominate members from the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha. The President could nominate a maximum of two members. By the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, by amending Article 334, the period of reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies was extended from 70 years to 80 years; however, the provision for nomination of Anglo-Indian members was rendered ineffective.

stem: Generally how many sessions are there in the lok Sabha?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Article 85 of the Constitution of India provides for the sessions, prorogation, and dissolution of Parliament. Under it, the President has the power to summon each House of Parliament from time to time; however, the session of Parliament must be summoned in such a manner that the interval between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next session is not more than six months. In other words, at least two sessions of Parliament must be held in a year. Generally, in India, three sessions of the Lok Sabha are held in a year— 1. Budget Session (February–May) 2. Monsoon Session (July–August/September) 3. Winter Session (November–December)

stem: What constitutes the definition of money bill under article 110 of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: The regulation of borrowings of money

expl: Under the provisions of Article 110 of the Constitution, imposing/abolishing/regulating taxes (including matters of refund), regulating the borrowing of money, and appropriation of money out of the Consolidated Fund of India—all are included in the definition of a Money Bill. stem: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution the Annual Financial Statement (Budget) is necessary to be laid before the Parliament ?
expl: Article 112 of the Indian Constitution relates to the Annual Financial Statement (Budget). Under Article 112(1), the President shall cause to be laid before both Houses of Parliament, in respect of every financial year, a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for that year, which is called the “Annual Financial Statement” (Budget).

stem: By whom are the expenses of the Parliament of India controlled?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More then one of the above

expl: Parliament is the supreme legislative body of India. The Indian Parliament consists of the President and two Houses—Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and Lok Sabha (House of the People). The President has the power to summon or prorogue either House of Parliament, and to dissolve the Lok Sabha. Financial authorisation relating to the Consolidated Fund of India, the Contingency Fund of India and the Public Account of India is given only by Parliament. Therefore, the expenditure of the Parliament of India is controlled by Parliament itself.

stem: Who presides over the joint session of the Parliament?
expl: Under Article 118(4) of the Constitution, at a joint sitting of the two Houses, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides; and in the Speaker’s absence, such person as may be determined by rules of procedure shall preside.

stem: What is the object of “cut motion” in Parliament ?

options.label: c

expl: A proposal moved in the lower House (Lok Sabha) to modify the Demands for Grants of the Union Budget is called a Cut Motion. Through it, the Demands for Grants presented for expenditure in the budget are considered improper, and a proposal is brought to reduce them. Cut Motions are of three types—Policy Cut Motion, Token Cut Motion and Economy Cut Motion.

stem: A seat of an M.P. can be declared vacant if he absents himself from the house for a continuous period of –

However, in computing this period, no account shall be taken of any period during which the House is prorogued or is adjourned for more than four consecutive days.

stem: The Speaker of the lok Sabha enjoys

options.label: a
options.text: The right to vote only in case of a tie

options.label: b
options.text: The right to vote like other members of the House

options.label: c
options.text: Two votes - one in ordinary course and the other in case of a tie

expl: Under Article 100(1), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha does not vote in the first instance on any matter; but if the votes are equally divided, the Speaker has and exercises a casting vote. Further, under Article 96(1), when a resolution for the Speaker’s removal is under consideration in the Lok Sabha, the Speaker shall not preside even if present; and under Article 96(2), in that situation, the Speaker shall have the right to vote in the first instance on that resolution, but shall not have the right to exercise a casting vote in case of equality of votes. On this basis, option (c) may also appear correct; however, option (a) is the more precise answer.

stem: Which Article of the Constitution restrict a Member of Parliament to hold the office of profit ?
expl: Article 102 (1) (a) of the Constitution bars a Member of Parliament from holding an office of profit. Under this Article, a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament if he holds any office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State, other than an office declared by Parliament by law not to disqualify its holder.

stem: The Rajya Sabha consists of-

options.label: d

expl: Article 80(1), sub-clauses (a) and (b) provide respectively that the Rajya Sabha shall consist of 12 members nominated by the President and not more than 238 representatives of the States and Union Territories (Total—250). Under Article 80(4), the representatives of each State in the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the Legislative Assembly of that State in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. Thus, their election is indirect, through representatives chosen by the citizens. Under Article 80(5), the representatives of the Union Territories in the Rajya Sabha shall be chosen in such manner as Parliament may by law prescribe.

stem: Of the following statements, which one is not correct?

options.label: a

expl: According to Article 109(1), a Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Rajya Sabha. Further, Article 109(2) states that the Rajya Sabha shall return the Money Bill to the Lok Sabha within 14 days, along with its recommendations. The Lok Sabha is not bound to accept the recommendations of the Rajya Sabha.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. The summoning of the House means convocation
2. Prorogation ends a session
3. Dissolution terminates a House
4. Prorogation of a session can be effected by the leader of the House alone Out of these which is not true?
expl: This question relates to the major procedures of the Indian Parliament/Legislature—Summoning, Adjournment, Prorogation, and Dissolution. Adjournment is done by the Presiding Officer/Speaker/Chairman (or the person acting as such), whereas prorogation is done by the President/Governor. Also, by adjournment, the House is adjourned for a definite or indefinite period; it does not end the session, i.e., it does not amount to prorogation. In fact, prorogation ends a session. note: In the statement (4) Prorogation of a session can be effected by the leader of the House alone is incorrect. So answer is option (d).

stem:
Joint Session of both the Houses of Parliament is concerned
1. For the election of the President of India
2. For the election of the vice-President of India
3. To pass the Bill relating to the amendment of Constitution
4. To discuss and pass such a Bill where both Houses have different opinion
Select your answer from the following code –
expl: According to Article 108 of the Constitution, a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament is held when there is a disagreement between the two Houses in considering and passing a Bill. The provision of a joint sitting under Article 108 applies only to ordinary Bills; it is not applicable to Money Bills and Constitution Amendment Bills. Under Article 118(4) (read with the rules made for joint sittings under Article 118(3)), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over the joint sitting. In the absence of the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides; and if he/she is also absent, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides. The joint sitting is conducted according to the rules for joint sitting made under Article 118(3). The quorum for a joint sitting is one-tenth of the total number of members of both Houses.

stem: How many members can the President nominate to the lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha respectively?
expl: Under Article 80, the President may nominate 12 persons to the Rajya Sabha who have special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, and social service. The original Article 331 provided that if the President was of the opinion that the Anglo-Indian community was not adequately represented in the Lok Sabha, he could nominate not more than two members of that community to the Lok Sabha. Thus, in the context of the question as asked at that time, the intended answer was option (b). However, after the Constitution (One Hundred and Fourth Amendment) Act, 2019 came into force (25 January 2020), the provision under Article 331 ceased to have effect, and now the President can nominate only 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.

stem: vote on Account is meant for -

options.label: a
options.text: Vote on the report of CAG

options.label: c
options.text: Appropriating funds pending passing of budget

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India only after the Appropriation Bill is passed. However, if there is a change in the government at the end of the financial year and the new government does not immediately introduce the Appropriation Bill, or if for any other reason money is needed even before the Appropriation Bill is passed, then under Article 116(1)(a) the Lok Sabha can pass a Vote on Account and approve an advance amount for the government. Article 116 also provides that if, in emergency circumstances, the government needs a very large amount of money—such as during war—then the Lok Sabha grants a Vote of Credit, and Parliament authorizes the withdrawal by law.

stem: The Public Accounts Committee submits its reports to-

options.label: b
options.text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

expl: The Public Accounts Committee submits its report to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, and it is presented in the Lok Sabha in the presence of the Speaker. The Public Accounts Committee is a parliamentary committee that exercises control over public expenditure. It consists of 22 members in total—15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha. Its purpose is to bring before the House the misuse and irregularities in public expenditure. It also recommends action against those public authorities who are found responsible for the misuse of public expenditure. The committee examines public expenditure on the basis of the CAG’s report. Generally, it has been the practice (since 1967) to appoint an opposition member of the Lok Sabha as its Chairperson. The Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

stem: Which of the following is a parliamentary committee relating to delegation of power to make rules and regulations of the executive?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/more than one of the above

expl: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation is related to the delegated power given to the executive to frame rules and regulations. The function of this parliamentary committee is to examine whether the powers conferred by the Constitution or delegated by Parliament—such as making rules, regulations, sub-rules, schemes, or other statutory instruments—are being properly exercised by the executive or not. Both Houses of Parliament have their own Committee on Subordinate Legislation, in which 15 members are nominated from the concerned House by the Speaker/Chairman, as the case may be.
